Taming flaky tests in CI

Flaky tests erode trust in the suite. When a test fails one run and passes the next, engineers learn to ignore red builds, and real regressions slip through unnoticed.

We started by measuring flakiness: every test result from the last thirty days went into a small database, and any test that both passed and failed on the same commit was marked as flaky. That gave us a ranked list of the worst offenders instead of a vague feeling.

Next we quarantined the flaky tests. They still run on every build, but their failures no longer block merges. Each quarantined test gets an owner and a ticket, and it leaves quarantine only after a week of green runs.

Most of the root causes were boring: shared state between tests, timing assumptions, and tests that depended on the order in which they ran. Fixing them took weeks, not months.
